definitions.explanation: The property or treatment of repelling water, causing it to bead up and roll off a surface rather than soaking in. Commonly used to describe fabric treatments and coatings.

examples.japanese: {撥水|はっすい}{加工|かこう}のジャケット。
この{生地|きじ}は{撥水|はっすい}{性|せい}に{優|すぐ}れている。
examples.english: This fabric has excellent water repellency.

examples.japanese: {撥水|はっすい}スプレーを{靴|くつ}に{吹|ふ}きかけておけば、{雨|あめ}の{日|ひ}でも{安心|あんしん}だ。
examples.english: If you spray water-repellent on your shoes, you can feel at ease even on rainy days.

notes:
Compound noun: {撥|はつ} (to repel) + {水|すい} (water). Often used as a modifier in compound forms.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {撥水|はっすい}{加工|かこう} (water-repellent treatment/finish)
- {撥水|はっすい}スプレー (water-repellent spray)
- {撥水|はっすい}{性|せい} (water repellency)
- {撥水|はっすい}{効果|こうか} (water-repellent effect)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {防水|ぼうすい}: waterproof — completely prevents water penetration
- {撥水|はっすい}: water-repellent — causes water to bead and roll off, but not fully waterproof
